<!-- pr-reviewer: af0f17478d8bbc86145ffc6eb1d4420745eddbad -->

**Verdict: Needs changes before merge.** The fix is right in its goal. The new eye distance is fixed at 100 mm, so the near clip plane can sit inside a large model. That breaks a case the old code handled.

## What looks good

- The perspective near-plane change is correct. `dist` already clamps to at least 0.5 mm (`viewport.rs:1118`), so the formula stays inside sane bounds at every zoom.
- The ortho dolly bug you describe is real: the eye travelled with `dist` into the model.
- The tests still hold. You updated the mode-switch test for the new eye. Good.
- The commit subject follows the conventional format.

## Results

Build and tests ran locally on Windows, in a trial merge with current main (058e14ca0). The merge is clean; no conflicts.

| Step | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib` | 774 passed, 0 failed, 5 ignored |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

Not exercised: the release-tier heavy lanes and the pixel-snapshot lanes (release-lane by law). No posted G-code, collision check, stock simulation math or geometry changed. This PR cannot alter NC output.

## Requested before merge

1. **The fixed eye can put the near clip plane inside the model.** In ortho the eye now sits 100 mm behind the target at every zoom (`viewport.rs:1323-1328`). The near plane stays about 0.1 mm in front of the eye, so it sits 99.9 mm in front of the target plane - always. Ortho framing shows everything the cone shows at the target plane, which is 0.577 * `dist` half-height, and `dist` clamps up to 100 000. So the view box reaches far past 100 mm, but the clip plane does not. Any nearer geometry fails the `0 <= z <= w` clip test: it disappears from the render, and ortho picks miss it too, because `ray_through` starts at the eye plane.
   Example: an ortho front view of a 300 mm long part, target at its centre. The front half sits in front of the eye plane, so it is invisible. The old code moved the eye with `dist`, so a zoomed-out view kept that geometry.
   Suggested fix: make the ortho near plane independent of the eye, and always in front of the visible box. In `mvp`, for the orthographic branch use for example `let near = -((self.dist * 20.0).max(1000.0) - ORTHO_EYE_DIST);`. `dist` cannot shrink past its 0.5 clamp, so this stays below zero and never reaches the eye. The `ORTHO_EYE_DIST` comment (`viewport.rs:1081-1087`) says nothing useful comes of pushing the eye toward the model. True - do not move the eye; move the plane instead. The test `the_ortho_depth_spans_zero_to_one_between_the_planes` (`law_tests.rs:2176`) repeats the near-plane formula in its own lines. Update it to the new formula, or that test fails.
2. **Add a test for that case.** A point at `target + 150 * back` (back = the eye direction), `dist = 300`, ortho: its clip `z / w` must stay inside [0, 1]. The current tests never put geometry in front of the eye plane, so none caught point 1.
3. **Add the missing body lines.** The PR body needs a `Changelog:` line, because the PR changes visible behavior. It also names no issue. If no issue covers this viewport bug yet, a maintainer will file one. This is housekeeping, not a code change.

## Notes (not blocking)

- `law_tests.rs:2239`: the comment says the hit point is "on the target plane". With the eye at 100 mm and `dist` at 80 mm, `origin + dir * dist` no longer sits on the target plane. The test still passes, because ortho rays are parallel. The plane-through-target form you added in the mode-switch test would fit here too.
- `viewport.rs` is 1501 lines. The project asks for a split at about 400 lines. This is not your PR's fault; we record the growth, we do not block on it.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

<!-- pr-reviewer: 48bfe892e15cc58fad265d9062b1e327030506d1 -->

**Verdict: The code is correct. The branch conflicts with main. The PR merges after a re-merge with main.**

This is a delta review. It covers the commits since `af0f1747` (the head of the last review). The review at that head asked for three changes. This review checks each one.

## The prior change request: met

1. Met. The ortho branch now uses `near = -((dist * 20.0).max(1000.0) - ORTHO_EYE_DIST)` (`viewport.rs:1415`). The plane always sits behind the eye plane, and never reaches the eye. `the_ortho_depth_spans_zero_to_one_between_the_planes` uses the same formula.
2. Met. `the_ortho_projection_keeps_a_point_in_front_of_the_eye_plane` tests `dist = 300` with a point 150 mm back from the target. It asserts `0 <= z / w <= 1` (`law_tests.rs:2175`).
3. Met. The body now has the `Changelog:` line. It says no issue covers the bug yet. A maintainer will file one.

Note: `6c41483fe` is not new code. The rebase rewrote the head that the last review read. The net code change since `af0f1747` is `48bfe892e` only.

## Results

The trial merge with `origin/main` (`6349a542e`) conflicts in code. One hunk: `eye()`. Main commit `c620c1255` added the `frame.to_world` rotation there. The PR changed the distance inside the same lines. The laws do not lose a rule in a resolution: the rotation keeps lengths, so the fixed 100 mm eye distance survives inside the rotated form. The author re-merges main into the branch (never a rebase) and puts `d` into the rotated offset.

Because of that conflict, the build ran on the PR head, not on a merged tree. It ran locally on Windows.

| Step | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib` | 803 passed, 0 failed, 5 ignored |
| `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib projection_tests` | 8 passed, 0 failed |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

Not exercised: the release-tier heavy lanes and the pixel-snapshot lanes (release-lane by law). No posted G-code, collision check, stock simulation math or geometry changed. This PR cannot alter NC output.

## Before merge

1. Re-merge `origin/main` into the branch and resolve the `eye()` hunk: keep main's `frame.to_world` form, and use the mode-selected `d` for the offset length. Push, then the refresh takes the normal merge path.

## Notes (not blocking)

- Picking and rendering now cover different depths in ortho. The near plane reaches about `20 * dist` behind the eye plane, so geometry more than 100 mm behind the target renders. But `ray_through` starts the ortho ray at the eye plane, so a click through a hole onto that far-back geometry finds no hit at `t >= 0`. The old code had the same split the other way round. This review suggests a follow-up issue (`P7`) to start the ortho pick ray at the near plane. It does not block this PR.
- `viewport.rs` is 1511 lines. The project asks for a split at about 400 lines. We record the growth, we do not block on it.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
